name: Jalapeño Salmon Bites in Crispy Rice Paper
desc: Soy and sriracha marinated salmon cubes wrapped with jalapeño and avocado in double layers of rice paper and pan-fried crisp.

source.title: Jalapeño Salmon Bites in Crispy Rice Paper
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 lb skinless salmon fillet, fresh or thawed, cut into 1 inch cubes
1 to 2 ripe avocados, cut into small wedges

steps: Toss the salmon cubes with the salt and smoked paprika.
Stir together the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, red pepper flakes and sriracha. Set aside 1/4 of it as a dipping sauce.
Toss the salmon with the remaining 3/4 of the marinade, cover and refrigerate at least 30 min and up to overnight.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Lift the salmon out of the marinade and fry until golden and cooked through (145°F), 3 to 4 min per side. Transfer to a plate and discard the used marinade.

Fill a shallow bowl with warm water. Dip a rice paper round for a few seconds until pliable and lay it flat. Place 2 salmon cubes, 1 jalapeño slice and 1 avocado wedge in the center, fold both sides toward the middle and roll into a small packet.
Soften a second rice paper round and wrap the packet again. Repeat with the rest to make 8 double-wrapped bites.

Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the bites in a single layer without crowding until crisp and browned, 3 to 4 min per side. Serve immediately with the reserved dipping sauce.
tips: The reel caption says to marinate 4 hours to overnight; the creator's written recipe says 30 min, with overnight preferred. Either works.
The dipping sauce is set aside before it touches the raw salmon, so it is safe to serve as is.
